result.title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World
result.summary: Underwater navigation requires translating visual spatial cues into motion, yet marine vision-language datasets rarely include paired robot trajectories. We present NereidVLA, a vision-language-action model that transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned 3D navigation. We first train Sea2Know on approximately two million marine examples to learn target grounding, spatial relations, and scene structure without paired robot-motion supervision. We then adapt it using expert trajectories executed under simulated underwater vehicle dynamics. Given RGB histories and a language instruction, NereidVLA predicts discrete motion tokens that decode into local 3D trajectories for closed-loop tracking. Evaluation combines an independent six-dimensional underwater navigation understanding benchmark with offline prediction and closed-loop navigation. Under matched navigation training and execution settings, marine spatial pretraining increases simulation success from 72.4% to 84.4%. Without fine-tuning on the real test environment, NereidVLA achieves 78.75% success in laboratory-pool robot trials, compared with 47.50% for InternVLA-N1. These results show that marine spatial supervision can support downstream motion learning and physical underwater navigation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 NereidVLA：先用约两百万海洋样本做空间知识预训练（Sea2Know），再用专家轨迹适配，将 RGB 历史与语言指令映射为离散运动 token 以解码 3D 轨迹进行闭环水下导航。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于机器人 VLA 任务应用，增益来自海洋空间预训练与轨迹监督，未涉及视觉细节如何在内部状态中保留、latent 推理状态生成或证据筛选与停止决策，缺少可供核查的 LVR 线索。
